name: DocSend
summary: Dropbox's secure document sharing and data room tool: send a deck or a data room as a tracked link, see page-by-page who read what, and gate access with email authentication, NDAs and watermarks.
best_for: founders sharing a pitch deck or running a fundraise, and small deal teams that want a data room with page-level analytics, NDA gating and watermarking without buying a legacy virtual data room
skip_if: you only need to send a PDF now and then (a shared drive link does that for free), you want month-to-month billing for a single short deal, or your team needs Salesforce or SSO and will not accept prices given only by sales
honest_knock:
The cheap plan is not the product people buy DocSend for. Personal at $10 a month tracks who opened a single document and for how long, but it has no data rooms at all. Sharing several files behind one link starts on Standard at $45 per user a month, and the controls that make a data room safe for a fundraise or a sale (visitor email authentication, watermarking, NDA gating, folder permissions) start on Advanced at $150 a month. Price the plan for the job you actually have, not the entry price on the page.

Monthly billing is expensive. The same Advanced plan costs $250 a month without a yearly commitment, two-thirds more than the $150 yearly rate, and Advanced Data Rooms goes from $180 to $300. A company that needs a data room for one four-month deal pays $1,000 on monthly billing, against $1,800 for a year it may not use. Work out that sum before you pick a toggle.

Several things a larger team will want are priced only through sales: the Salesforce integration, single sign-on and sub-teams. The trial is 14 days of the top plan, but visitors are capped during it, so a trial is not the place to run the real fundraise. We have not used DocSend ourselves; the figures here come from its pricing page and plan tooltips.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Personal · per user per month billed yearly ($15 billed monthly), one user, no data rooms
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-25 on docsend.com/pricing, both billing toggles) Personal is $10 per user a month billed yearly or $15 billed monthly, one user, basic link controls (email to view, passcode, expiry, download on or off), document-level analytics, 4 eSignatures a month, unlimited visitors and 10 GB of storage. Standard is $45 per user a month yearly or $65 monthly and adds multi-file sharing through data rooms (Spaces) of up to 200 assets each, video analytics, file requests, custom branding with a branded subdomain, unlimited eSignature and 50 GB per user. Advanced is $150 a month yearly or $250 monthly for three users, with extra users at $60 a month yearly or $90 monthly, and adds folder structure in Spaces, visitor email authentication, allow and block lists, folder and file permissions, dynamic watermarking and NDA gating, with 2,000 assets per data room. Advanced Data Rooms is $180 a month yearly or $300 monthly for three users on the same extra-user rate, and adds group visitor permissions, due diligence tracking, a data room audit log, automatic file indexing, data room analytics, priority email support and 4,000 assets per data room. Yearly billing saves 33% on Personal, 31% on Standard and 40% on the two team plans. Salesforce is a paid add-on from Standard up, SSO (Okta, OneLogin, Azure) and sub-teams are paid add-ons on the two team plans, all priced only through sales. Data rooms and visitors are unlimited on every plan that has them; uploads are capped at 2 GB per file. The free trial is 14 days of Advanced Data Rooms, and unlimited visitors are not available during it. Sales tax is added in jurisdictions where Dropbox is registered. Separately, the DocSend startups page offers new customers one year at 90% off an annual Standard or Advanced plan with up to $2 million raised, 50% off with up to $10 million, and 20% off annual Advanced with up to $20 million.

compare_with.name: a shared Google Drive or Dropbox link
compare_with.why: the free default most people start with. A drive link gets the file to the reader and can be switched off, but it does not tell you which pages an investor read, for how long, or whether they forwarded it, and it cannot put an NDA or a per-viewer watermark in front of the document. That tracking and gating is what DocSend charges for, from $10 a month for one document owner to $150 a month for a three-person deal team. If you would not act on the page-by-page data, the drive link is enough.
